What changed in the current release. The version this guide was built for is shown in the footer.

KTPH000Main windows now reopen at their remembered position on macOSKTPH001 — the native unified title bar could move a window after korTTY restored its saved bounds, making every restart appear lower even though the new position had been stored. korTTY now reapplies normal bounds after the native window is ready and also recovers main-window positions left on a disconnected monitor.

KTPH000Every user-resizable application window now remembers its geometryKTPH001 — main windows and named dialogs persist their position and size separately, tool tabs continue to follow their main window, and a dialog moved onto a disconnected monitor is recovered onto an available screen.

KTPH000The German JobScheduler interface is now fully localizedKTPH001 — its tabs, fields, action and status names, target and remote-data selectors, security prompts, journal controls, validation messages and errors no longer mix German menus with English dialog content.

KTPH000All seven AtlantaFX application designsKTPH001 — the Appearance tab now places AtlantaFX 2.1.0's Primer Dark, Primer Light, Nord Dark, Nord Light, Cupertino Dark, Cupertino Light and Dracula themes at the top of the design list. New installations start with Primer Dark, existing selections are not migrated, switching to a non-AtlantaFX design restores Modena explicitly, and open windows, dialogs and popups update immediately while terminal, Monaco, journal and chat colors remain independent.

KTPH000Four new AI diagram typesKTPH001 — besides the logical-structure flowchart, the snippet editor can now generate KTPH002sequenceKTPH003, KTPH004stateKTPH005, KTPH006classKTPH007, and KTPH008ERKTPH009 diagrams. Each family uses its own compact, safety-restricted Mermaid dialect and its own built-in quality skill, and renders in the bundled offline Mermaid renderer as before. See KTPH010Mermaid diagramsKTPH011.

KTPH000Several diagrams per snippetKTPH001 — a snippet now stores any number of diagrams. The diagram window lists them with family, title, and line range, offers KTPH002New diagramKTPH003 with a type choice, and can KTPH004DeleteKTPH005 a selected diagram; KTPH006RegenerateKTPH007 keeps each diagram's family and scope.

KTPH000Diagram from a selectionKTPH001 — select part of a script and pick a diagram type from the editor's new KTPH002Generate diagramKTPH003 context submenu to diagram just those lines. The diagram remembers the line range, its code references point at the real snippet lines, and regeneration re-reads the same lines.

KTPH000Diagrams no longer fail on thinking modelsKTPH001 — the diagram request's output budget covered the model's hidden reasoning as well, so a reasoning model could use up the whole budget before writing a single character of the diagram, and generation failed after minutes of work. The budget now leaves room for that reasoning, and a response that is still cut off says so instead of reporting a generic failure.

KTPH000A rejected AI flow diagram now says soKTPH001 — when korTTY discarded an AI-generated flowchart, the KTPH002Full code analysisKTPH003 window silently showed the generic local fallback diagram instead, so a long script always seemed to produce a trivial five-node chart. The fallback now carries a notice naming the rejection reason, the same reason appears in the editor's status line and in the log together with the diagram's node and edge counts, and a diagram whose nodes lack a valid source mapping is kept (those nodes merely lose their hover reference) instead of being replaced by the fallback.

KTPH000Flow diagrams of long scripts are less generic and generate much fasterKTPH001 — the diagram request never told the model the node limit that the validator enforced, so for a script of several thousand lines the model transcribed the whole script into hundreds of nodes, spent minutes doing it, and was rejected. The limit is now part of the request and grows with the script — 12 action/decision nodes for snippets up to 200 lines, up to 24 at 1,000 lines or more — and the built-in flowchart skill asks for the main phases of a long script rather than every branch. A script longer than 400 lines is also sent as a condensed structural outline — its definitions and top-level flow, with elided runs marked and the original line numbers kept — instead of every single line, which cuts the request size several-fold and lets the model describe phases instead of statements. See KTPH002Mermaid diagramsKTPH003.

KTPH000Full code analysis can now be applied to long scriptsKTPH001 — each apply stage used to return the complete rewritten script as a JSON array of every line. For a 4,000-line script that is around 60,000 output tokens: at the model's completion cap, twelve minutes per stage, and a single lost quotation mark in that much JSON lost all of it — with MiniMax-M3 every stage failed after 18 minutes. Above 400 lines a stage now receives the line-numbered snippet and returns only the changed regions, which korTTY applies locally before running exactly the same verification as before; untrustworthy ranges are refused, the log names what was applied, and the stage's output cap drops to 32,768 tokens. Short snippets keep the proven whole-file answer. See KTPH002Full code analysisKTPH003.

KTPH005Flow diagrams now accept the Mermaid that models actually writeKTPH006 — tested live against MiniMax-M3, korTTY's diagram grammar rejected one answer in three for shorthand the contract never allowed but every model uses: nodes declared inline in an edge, chained edges, KTPH000 labels, the KTPH001 shorthand, unquoted labels, other node shapes, and the model's own slips (a label pipe typed as a bracket, a shape closed early, a decision drawn as a diamond with one exit, a mistyped id left dangling, KTPH002 in a label tripping the URL screen). The grammar now reads all of these and rewrites an accepted diagram into its strict dialect before rendering or saving, the validator tolerates a modest overshoot of the stated node limit instead of discarding a summarized diagram, the contract shows the edge-label syntax instead of describing it, and only what cannot be drawn faithfully — parallel branches from one action — is still rejected, with the reason named. A KTPH003 the model declared but never connected is wired to the flow's real entry, statements written with a stray KTPH004 prefix are still read, and a repaired diagram that kept fewer than half of the drawn nodes is refused rather than shown as a stub.

KTPH004A diagram is no longer rejected for the colors a model added to itKTPH005 — the diagram contract tells the model to assign four semantic classes that korTTY styles itself, and a model that reads "class" often reaches for KTPH000 and defines them with colors as well. The security screen then refused a complete, correct diagram for its decoration. Such KTPH001, KTPH002 and KTPH003 lines are now dropped from a fresh answer before validation (the log says how many), the contract says explicitly not to define the classes, and a saved diagram is still validated unchanged.

KTPH009MiniMax no longer thinks through diagram requestsKTPH010 — korTTY pins the diagram request to the KTPH000 reasoning value, but MiniMax ignores KTPH001 and only its own KTPH002 parameter switches reasoning off; KTPH003 therefore arrived as no parameter at all and MiniMax-M3 reasoned by default, billing the hidden thinking as completion tokens (4,853 of them for a 130-line script) and opening the reply with an inline KTPH004 block. Both KTPH011DisabledKTPH012 and KTPH005 now send KTPH006 to MiniMax. The flowchart validator also accepts chained edges (KTPH007) and plain KTPH008 comments as the shorthand they are, quotes the offending line when it still has to reject one, skips inline reasoning before recovering a diagram from a broken answer, and logs the answer length beside the token count so hidden reasoning can be told from a verbose reply.

KTPH000A diagram is no longer lost to a misplaced quotation markKTPH001 — korTTY's diagram grammar requires quoted node labels, and those quotes have to survive inside the JSON string a model returns. Models regularly lost that escaping on longer answers, and a complete, perfectly good diagram was discarded because the surrounding JSON no longer parsed. korTTY now constrains the diagram answer with its own JSON schema over OpenAI-compatible HTTP, and recovers the diagram from the answer's own text when the envelope is unreadable anyway — also from a compact single-line answer whose remaining fields follow the diagram on the same line — validated exactly as before, and without ever repeating the request.

KTPH007Applying a full code analysis to a long script costs half the prompt tokensKTPH008 — every apply stage sends the whole line-numbered script, so the number of stages is what a run costs, and on a 4,009-line script each stage was around 63,000 prompt tokens. Edit-mode stages now take six analysis items instead of three: the three-item limit exists so that a whole-script answer stays finishable, and an edit-mode answer holds only the changed regions. Measured live with MiniMax-M3 on that script, twelve analysis items went from four stages to two — 126,391 prompt tokens instead of roughly 252,000, all twelve edits applied — and the progress window plans with the same stage size. Hardening batches are unchanged. Two more things remove the schemaless retry that used to re-send the whole script: an edit-mode answer whose JSON does not parse is now read tolerantly and locally — the slips seen live from MiniMax-M3 are an unescaped quotation mark inside a code line, an escape JSON does not know such as KTPH000, a missing KTPH001 before an edit's closing brace, a newline inside an entry, and the summary written as a nested object; the read is all edits or none, so a half-readable answer still goes the retry route — and endpoints that accept KTPH002 and ignore it, such as MiniMax, get the retry's JSON-only reminder with the first attempt. When a retry does happen, the log now names how the first answer failed (unparsable JSON, cut off, fenced, prose), and the request log shows the prompt tokens an endpoint served from its prefix cache when it reports them, and every answer korTTY could not use is kept complete under KTPH003 in the log directory (the twenty most recent), with the log line naming the file and the place the JSON broke, so a failed stage can be diagnosed from a report without debug logging. The edit-mode parser also read every replacement line through the identifier-list parser, which trimmed indentation, dropped blank lines and removed a repeated KTPH004 or KTPH005 inside one edit; replacement lines are now taken verbatim. Two more edit-mode guards come from the same live runs: a hollow edit — a range of three or more lines "replaced" by its own first line, which would have gutted a function and was accepted as applied — is dropped, its echoed id is ignored so the repair round asks for the item, and a stage none of whose edits can be applied gets one second attempt that says what was wrong instead of failing the run at once. The analysis answer is repaired when a raw quote pair sits inside one of its prose fields — a live 24,000-character analysis was lost to KTPH006 inside one suggestion — and an analysis korTTY still cannot use is archived with the log line naming the file.

KTPH000AI chat answers now display formatted MarkdownKTPH001 — headings, emphasis, lists, quotations, and inline code appear as a readable preview alongside the existing tables and code blocks. Long text wraps without a fixed-height inner scrollbar. The conversation follows new messages and delayed layout changes, pauses when you scroll up, and resumes when you return to the bottom.

KTPH000AI chat PDF exports preserve symbols and emojiKTPH001 — Unicode characters such as check marks, stars, smileys and icons are now rendered with embedded fallback fonts instead of being replaced with question marks, and remain searchable text in the PDF.

KTPH000AI code actions no longer translate your script's commentsKTPH001 — every action that rewrites code used to force the snippet's comments, messages, log lines and help text into the configured KTPH002Text languageKTPH003, which defaults to korTTY's own interface language. Running korTTY in German and applying a KTPH004Full code analysisKTPH005 result to an English script therefore translated the whole file's prose, without asking. korTTY now keeps the language the script is already written in and only writes new text to match. Translating is still available — select a language under KTPH006Text languageKTPH007 — but it is now something you ask for. Where korTTY cannot tell which language a script uses, because there is too little text or the comments mix languages, it asks once per snippet instead of guessing. This applies to Full code analysis, security fixes, the improve and assist actions, alternatives, one-liners and code completion.

KTPH000The KTPH001Full code analysisKTPH002 review preview no longer freezes korTTYKTPH003 — while the preview of a finished run was open, no terminal session accepted input and the processing window beside it could not even be scrolled, because the preview blocked the whole application. It no longer does: your sessions keep running and you can read what the run did while you review its result. Since the snippet can now be edited during the review, korTTY checks before applying that the editor still holds the text the result came from, and refuses rather than overwriting newer edits.

KTPH000The analysis, processing and preview windows now dock into one surfaceKTPH001 — the review preview attaches to the free side of the KTPH002Full code analysisKTPH003 window and the AI-processing window to the other, both matching its height and following it as it moves. korTTY makes room by sliding the analysis window, and narrows it only when all three cannot fit side by side. Each docked window can be resized and its width is remembered; dragging one away detaches it, and KTPH004Arrange windowsKTPH005 lays all three out again.

KTPH000The processing window now stays open with a run summaryKTPH001 — it used to disappear together with the preview, taking the numbers with it. It now remains, reporting the run's duration, the prompt/completion/total token usage, the AI profile used, how many work items completed and how many repair attempts were needed, with KTPH002Copy summaryKTPH003 and KTPH004Show preview againKTPH005. Closing the analysis window clears the group.

KTPH000New category icons in the analysis reportKTPH001 — Security, Optimization, Design and Dependencies are marked by a padlock, a gauge, stacked layers and a module hexagon. The previous set was hard to read at a glance; "Design" in particular was a water drop, which said nothing about code structure. The same icons are used in the report, the processing checklist, the review preview's explanation cards and the exported HTML and PDF.

KTPH000KTPH001Full code analysisKTPH002 no longer fails on some local reasoning modelsKTPH003 — when korTTY requests a strictly structured result from a local server, certain reasoning models return their complete answer in the reasoning channel and leave the actual reply empty. korTTY treated this as an empty reply and discarded a finished analysis after minutes of work. korTTY now detects such a reply and uses the analysis it already contains. Only if that text is unusable does it ask a second time, without the strict format. This was observed with the newer Qwen reasoning models in LM Studio, and it affected KTPH004Full code analysisKTPH005 and KTPH006Apply selectedKTPH007 in the snippet editor. Models that return a normal reply are unaffected.

KTPH000The Terminal Effects manager window can now be resizedKTPH001 — expanding the window gives the plugin names and descriptions more room while preserving the live preview; installations that open tool windows as tabs continue to use the available main-window area.

KTPH002Open in Snippet Editor no longer resolves the wrong path after a user switchKTPH003 — after switching identity inside a session, with KTPH000 for example, or an KTPH001 typed into a local shell, the context-menu entry resolved a selected file name against the original login's directories and loaded nothing, or a wrong same-named file. The entry is now greyed out while the session runs as a different identity and re-enables on its own once the prompt shows the original user again. See KTPH004Local shell tabsKTPH005.

KTPH000A split no longer asks again for the reason of the connectionKTPH001 — when a server wants a reason for the operation, as a CyberArk-style jump host does, every split of a tab opened that dialog again although the reason had been given when the tab was opened. korTTY now sends the answer already given in that tab. It is still sent rather than skipped, because a server that asks for a reason closes a session that answers with nothing. A split to a different server, or a server asking something else, is asked once as well, and a new tab always starts by asking. If the server refuses the reason, because a ticket number has expired in the meantime for example, korTTY drops it and asks again. See KTPH002Split-screen with broadcastKTPH003.

KTPH000Windows ARM no longer opens blank windows under x64 emulationKTPH001 — korTTY now detects an x64 JavaFX runtime running on ARM64 Windows and selects the reliable software renderer before JavaFX starts. Native Windows x64 installations retain hardware rendering.

KTPH004Native Flatpak bundles for Intel/AMD and ARM LinuxKTPH005 — GitHub releases now provide KTPH000 bundles for KTPH001 and KTPH002. A Flatpak installation stays on the Flatpak update path, verifies the downloaded GitHub asset and shows the host-terminal installation command instead of offering an incompatible distro package. Local shells and their AI-agent commands run on the host through KTPH003.

KTPH002Pacman packages for Arch Linux and Arch Linux ARMKTPH003 — release builds now package and verify both KTPH000 and KTPH001 application images. A guarded Pacman-only backfill can first produce inspection artifacts and later publish collision-free signed packages without replacing older release assets.

KTPH000Every korTTY package now identifies the application licence as MITKTPH001 — the Arch package previously declared Apache-2.0 even though korTTY's repository licence is MIT. Arch and RPM metadata now declare MIT, and every Java, native and Flatpak artifact contains the canonical licence file; third-party licences remain unchanged.

Only the current release is listed here, so the guide stays short in every language it is translated into. Every version is on the KTPH002GitHub releases pageKTPH003; the curated notes for earlier versions are kept in the repository, in KTPH000 and KTPH001.
